start.title: Getting started
start.desc: First steps: connect your keys and switch on the paid features.

app.title: Working in the app
app.desc: Trends, video generation, notebooks and the media library — how to use each section.

first-launch.title: First launch
first-launch.excerpt: How to connect your keys in Enterprise settings and switch on video, images, voiceover, avatars and trends.
first-launch.lead: TrendTraffic runs on the “bring your own key” model: every paid or cloud step (AI video, images, voiceover, avatars, trend scanning) uses your own provider key, stored encrypted. The free CPU chain (trimming, subtitles, export) needs no keys at all. All keys live in one place — Enterprise settings. Below is what each tab does and how to set it up.

intro.title: What Enterprise settings are and how to open them
intro.body:
Enterprise settings gather all integrations, keys and AI parameters for your account in one screen. Open it from the gear icon at the bottom of the left sidebar, or go straight to app.trendtraffic.pro/settings/enterprise. The section is available on the Enterprise plan (and to the superadmin).

Every key is stored encrypted and shown masked (for example AIzaSy…***). You can re-check or delete any key at any time — nothing is used without your action.
examples: Open settings: click the gear icon at the bottom of the left sidebar.
Don't see the section? It is Enterprise-only — check your plan on the Pricing page (/billing).
Every card has Save, Check/Validate and Delete — a key never leaves your account and can be removed in one click.

api.title: API — your Google Gemini key
api.body:
The API tab holds your personal Google Gemini key from AI Studio. Gemini is the analytical brain of the platform: frame-by-frame video analysis, transcripts, translation and text generation. Your key is used instead of the shared platform key for every Gemini call on your account.

The same tab also holds Quest Flow API keys (secrets for HTTP blocks), the image-generation model selector (for example Nano Banana or Imagen) and a Telegram bot token for notifications.
api.keyLabel: Get a key in Google AI Studio
examples: Paste the AI Studio key and press “Save and validate” — the status turns to “Active”.
Analyse a trend video frame by frame (Gallery → open a video → Analysis) — it runs on your Gemini quota.
Choose “Nano Banana (2.5 Flash Image)” as the image model for generating and editing pictures.
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token — get a Telegram message when auto-runs finish or a key stops working.

mcp.title: MCP — connect Claude and external AI agents
mcp.body:
Manage TrendTraffic from Claude in plain text: trends, gallery, audience, publisher. One-time setup in the “Claude Connector (MCP)” card in your regular Settings: press “Create personal key” (shown only once) and copy the two fields — the Name and the connector URL (the key is already inside the URL).

Method 1 — in the Claude app (recommended, no terminal): bottom left, click your profile and open settings → pick “Connectors” in the left column → top right “Add”, then “Add custom connector” → paste the name and URL, leave the OAuth fields empty, click “Add” → in a new chat type: “check the connection with TrendTraffic”.

Other methods live in the same card: the “Download MCP for Claude” button (a ready claude_desktop_config.json for Claude Desktop) and a one-line command for Claude Code. Fine-grained permissions (scopes for n8n, ChatGPT connectors or custom agents) are on the MCP tab of Enterprise settings; deleting a key instantly cuts off that integration.
examples: Settings → “Claude Connector (MCP)” → “Create personal key” → copy the “Name” and the “connector URL”.
In the Claude app: profile → settings → “Connectors” → “Add” → “Add custom connector” → paste the two fields (OAuth empty) → “Add”.
Test it: in a new chat type “check the connection with TrendTraffic” — Claude sees your trends, gallery and publisher.

Claude Desktop: the “Download MCP for Claude” button gives a ready claude_desktop_config.json (Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\), then restart Claude Desktop. Claude Code: the one-line command from the card.
For n8n or ChatGPT, create a separate key with only the scopes you need on the Enterprise → MCP tab; rotation: delete a key — access stops at once.

tikhub.title: Tikhub — your Trend key
tikhub.body: The Tikhub tab stores your own TikHub.io key for scanning trends and downloading videos from TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. It is used instead of the shared key, on your own quota. The Validate button calls TikHub live and shows the status and remaining balance.
examples: Paste the Trend key and press “Validate” — check the status and your remaining balance.
Scan trends by region and audience (Gallery → Trends) on your own quota.
Paste a TikTok / Instagram / YouTube link into Trends search to download and auto-analyse the video.
Analyse every video of a channel at once (Channels) — powered by the same key.

generation.title: Generation — the extension and render keys
generation.body:
The Generation tab holds the keys for paid or cloud rendering steps: AI video, images, voiceover and avatars. The free CPU chain (trimming, subtitles, formatting, export) needs no keys.

At the top is the TrendTraffic browser extension — one extension for both Google Flow (Veo) and NotebookLM. Below it, the AI Director (Anthropic Claude) — the brain behind smart script steps: research, best-moment selection, scripts and news (default Claude Opus). Then the paid providers: FAL.ai, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, HeyGen and more. Each provider card has Save, Check and Delete.
examples: Install the extension (“Download extension”) to unlock free Veo video through Google Flow and the Hotebook block.
Add an Anthropic Claude key (console.anthropic.com) — it powers scripts, research and news in the smart LLM nodes.
Add ElevenLabs (voiceover, music, SFX) and HeyGen (avatars) keys for the UGC studio.
Add FAL.ai (FLUX, Veo, Kling, MiniMax) for AI image and video generation.
No keys yet? The free CPU chain still trims, subtitles, formats and exports without any provider key.

hotebook.title: Hotebook — Google NotebookLM
hotebook.body:
The Hotebook tab connects the Hotebook block to your own Google NotebookLM through the same TrendTraffic extension, running in your browser under your Google login. Each account has its own connection and its own limits. The status shows one of: connected, extension offline, or sign-in needed.

Tip: use a separate Google account with a Google AI plan — the daily NotebookLM limits (audio / video / chat) are counted per account. The platform never stores your Google cookies; the login stays in your browser.
examples: Install the extension, open notebooklm.google.com and sign in — the “TrendTraffic → Hotebook” panel appears.
Generate audio or video overviews from your sources and pull the results into the Gallery.
Keep the NotebookLM tab open while the block works — sources, chat and generation run inside it.
Press “Check” on this tab if the status is stuck — it re-reads the live connection.

trends.title: Trends
trends.excerpt: Find viral videos, target your audience, analyse by link and track channels.
trends.lead: The Trends section finds viral videos on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and X — and analyses them. Four tabs: Search, Audience targeting, Analytics and Channels.

search.title: Search — find viral videos
search.body: The Search tab builds a feed of trends. Choose the sources (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X), the By keyword or Trending mode, and optionally a region, the number of videos (10/20/30), the search type (Smart search), sorting and period. The Scan button builds the feed. The Auto-analysis block runs on a schedule: it scans, takes one new video, analyses it and (optionally) assembles a UGC clip from a template.
examples: Type a keyword (e.g. “morning routine”) and press “Scan”.
The “Trending” mode returns fresh viral videos without a keyword.
Set a region and the number of videos to narrow the results.
Enable “Auto-analysis” (e.g. daily) — the platform finds and analyses a fresh trend by itself.

audience.title: Audience targeting — a map of micro-niches
audience.body: The Audience targeting tab starts from your product: describe what you promote and your core audience — the AI picks micro-niches and keywords and finds relevant videos for each. That means less competition and more precise targeting. Don't know your audience? Describe the product and press Suggest and the AI fills it in. One click builds the niches, finds the videos and ranks them by demand; then use the To TrendFlow button on the niche you want.
examples: Describe the product and press “Suggest” — the AI fills in the audience and keywords.
“Build audience map” — niches are ranked by demand (#1/#2/#3).
Choose a region and the keyword language (several at once is allowed).
The “Validate keywords” toggle uses real TikTok/YouTube queries instead of AI guesses.

analytics.title: Analytics — analyse a video by link
analytics.body: The Analytics tab breaks down any video by link: paste a TikTok / Instagram / YouTube URL and press Analyze — Gemini analyses it frame by frame (speech, scenes, hooks). The Add to gallery button saves the video and the breakdown into Media files. Videos found on the Search tab open here too.
examples: Paste a video link and press “Analyze”.
“Add to gallery” — the video and breakdown (.md + subtitles) go to Media files → “Analytics”.
Open a video from Search — it shows up here for analysis.

channels.title: Channels — track competitors
channels.body: The Channels tab watches channels: paste a TikTok / Instagram / YouTube channel URL. Track adds the channel to your list with daily auto-updates of its metrics (showing “was → is” changes). One-time analysis shows all of the channel's videos right now, without history.
examples: “Track” — watch a competitor's channel: followers and metrics update daily.
“One-time analysis” — all of the channel's videos at once, without keeping history.
The cards show the follower count and the time of the last update.

google-flow.title: Google Flow
google-flow.excerpt: Generate Veo videos in Google Flow through the TrendTraffic extension.
google-flow.lead: The Google Flow block generates Veo videos right inside Google Flow through the TrendTraffic browser extension: a prompt queue and exchange of finished videos with the Gallery.

use.title: How to connect and generate
use.body: Install the TrendTraffic extension (the button on the banner), open labs.google/flow and sign in to Google — the extension connects automatically as long as you're logged into the app. The Add tile sends a prompt/reference into the queue; finished videos appear in the Gallery and in Media files. If the status says the extension is offline, use the Reconnect button.
examples: Install the extension (the “Download” / “Update” banner) and sign in at labs.google/flow.
The “Add” tile — send a prompt or reference into the generation queue.
Finished Veo videos arrive in the Gallery and Media files by themselves.
“Reconnect” on the banner — if the extension connection drops.

hotebook.title: Hotebook
hotebook.excerpt: Google NotebookLM through the extension: sources, chat, audio and video overviews.
hotebook.lead: The Hotebook block is your own Google NotebookLM through the TrendTraffic extension. Work inside NotebookLM itself (sources, chat, generation), and finished studio outputs appear automatically in “Media files” (video/audio/images) and on this tab.

use.title: Working with notebooks
use.body: Install the extension and sign in at notebooklm.google.com. Your notebooks are listed here; click a notebook to open it in NotebookLM — that's where you work. While something is generating, a spinner turns on the card; finished audio and video overviews land in Media files by themselves. Generation runs under your own Google account and its limits (it can be separate from the app account).
examples: Install the extension, sign in at notebooklm.google.com — your notebooks appear here.
Click a notebook — it opens in NotebookLM, and you work right there.
Generate an audio or video overview — it arrives in Media files by itself.
“Refresh” updates the list; a spinner on a card means generation is running.

media-files.title: Media files
media-files.excerpt: The media library: all your videos, images, audio and breakdowns in one place.
media-files.lead: Media files is your account's single media library: everything finished flows here — UGC-studio clips, Google Flow videos, NotebookLM outputs, Analytics breakdowns.

use.title: Media library: filters, publishing, downloading
use.body: Switch the type: video / image / audio / analytics; search by name, author or description. Tick files (or Select all) and download them or send them to the Publisher. Every card has quick buttons: play, add to gallery, publish, delete, download.
examples: The “video / image / audio” filter shows only the type of file you need.
“Select all” → “Download” — grab a batch of files at once.
“Publish” — send a clip to the Publisher (social networks).
The “Analytics” sub-filter — saved video breakdowns (.md + subtitles).

ugc.title: UGC studio
ugc.excerpt: Talking-avatar clips: 4 video modes, formats, subtitles, music and templates.
ugc.lead: The UGC studio assembles clips with a talking person: an avatar (HeyGen) + a voice (ElevenLabs) + your footage + subtitles. Open it from the Gallery: the UGC tab → the “Add” tile (or click a saved clip’s card — its scenario continues right where you left off). Steps are on the left, a live preview of every format is on the right: you can drag and resize the avatar right on the frame. An approximate build price is shown in the header before you start.

overview.title: How the studio is organised
overview.body:
The build goes step by step: 1 Video mode → 2 Avatar → 3 Voice and text → 4 Video → 5 Subtitles → 6 Music → 7 Overlay. Formats are multi-select: 9:16 (TikTok/Reels/Shorts), 16:9 (YouTube), 1:1 and 4:5 (Instagram/Facebook feed) — one run produces a file for every selected format, and the avatar position is tuned per format.

The “Trend analysis” block plugs a breakdown from Analytics (trend DNA) into the build — tick what to reuse: the script, the trend’s video in your footage, the subtitle style, the montage direction. Header buttons: Save, Template (upserted on exit — the trend autopilot runs on it) and Brand kit. At the bottom of the panel is the “READY TO BUILD” checklist: what is still missing before the “Create video” button. Rendering runs on the server — you can close the window; the finished clip appears on the UGC tab and in Media files.
examples: Gallery → UGC → “Add” — a new build; click a clip’s card to continue its scenario.
Tick 9:16 and 16:9 together — you get a TikTok file and a YouTube file in one run.
Attach a “Trend analysis” — the script and subtitles are built from the viral video’s DNA.
Press “Exit” — the clip is saved and its template updated (the trend autopilot can run on it).

solo.title: Mode 1 — Solo presenter
solo.body:
The avatar speaks the entire script, with your footage alongside. The simplest option. Avatar source: “Ready-made avatars” (generate 3 from a text description or pick from your collection/gallery), “My photo” (HeyGen animates the portrait: lips and expressions sync with the voice; you can also pick a ready look from your HeyGen account) or “Pre-recorded video” — an already-shot clip of a talking person (HeyGen and ElevenLabs are not involved).

Layout: the avatar goes top / bottom / as a small overlay — then just drag and resize it on the preview (the position is remembered per format). Options: “Cut out avatar background (AI)” — only the person’s silhouette stays on screen; “Avatar over inserts” — the presenter stays visible while a media insert plays. Face rendering: a HeyGen API key (Settings → Generation, ~$3/min) or a HeyGen subscription via the extension. “Series languages”: Claude translates the script, ElevenLabs voices it — a separate finished clip per language.
examples: Describe the avatar (“25-year-old woman, casual”) → “Generate 3 avatars” → pick the best one.
“My photo” — upload a full-face portrait: HeyGen animates it and syncs the lips with the voiceover.
Drag the avatar into a corner and shrink it — the classic “talking head over a screencast” look.
Enable “Cut out avatar background (AI)” — the presenter’s silhouette sits right on top of your video, no rectangle.
Add series languages (e.g. en+es+de) — one script produces three localised clips.

retention.title: Mode 2 — Dynamic montage
retention.body:
Shots change every few seconds over a single voice track — viewers watch to the end. Works with “My photo” only. Montage intensity: Economy (~2 paid close-ups — the hook and the call to action), Balance (~3 — hook, action, CTA) and Premium (~4 — maximum face time, livelier and pricier).

The AI builds the shot plan from your text: Hook → Bridge → Cutaway → Action → Call to action. Purple segments are paid close-ups (HeyGen Avatar IV), “$0” segments are face-off shots (b-roll). Click a segment to preview the shot. Batch: add several B-roll videos — you get several clips while the avatar is paid for once.
examples: Start with “Balance” — the sweet spot of price and liveliness (~$2–3 per clip).
Paste your text — the AI decides where a close-up goes and where a $0 cutaway is enough.
Click the plan segments under the preview to see how each shot will look.
Upload 4 different B-rolls — you get 4 clips with one voiceover and one avatar payment.

dialogue.title: Mode 3 — Two-person dialogue
dialogue.body:
Two people talk with their own faces. You need two photos (Speaker A and Speaker B) and a recording of a two-voice conversation: switch to “My recording” and press “Transcribe speech” — the service splits the lines into voices A/B (diarisation).

Engagement: “Calm” (almost always one speaker on screen — the cheapest), “Balance” (a close-up of the speaker; both in frame on reactions and peaks), “Lively” (more “both in frame” scenes and inserts — more dynamic and pricier). The AI builds the dialogue plan: A closeup / Both in frame (the reaction is a static photo, $0) / B closeup / Background + face (a cut-out silhouette over media). The “Cut out background” option puts the speakers’ silhouettes over your footage.
examples: Upload two portraits (A and B) and a conversation recording — “Transcribe speech” splits the lines by voice.
Record the dialogue on your phone’s voice recorder — any recording with two audible voices works.
“Balance” engagement: both faces appear on reactions — lively without overpaying.
“Both in frame” scenes use a static reaction photo — those shots are free ($0).

voiceover.title: Mode 4 — No avatar — voiceover
voiceover.body: Your video + a voice: an AI-written script (voiced by ElevenLabs) or your own recording used as is. HeyGen is not involved — nearly free. A video is required (from the Gallery or a photo slideshow); media inserts per line are optional. Your own recording goes through loudness normalisation (loudnorm). “Series languages” work here too: one script — several localised clips.
examples: A screencast + an AI voiceover from a brief — a ready tutorial without filming a face.
Paste your text and press “Use my text as is” — the lines go to voiceover without AI processing.
Record the voice yourself — loudnorm evens out the recording volume.
A photo slideshow + a voice + word-by-word subtitles — the cheapest clip format.

steps.title: Steps 4–7: footage, subtitles, music, overlay
steps.body:
Video: a clip from the Gallery or a photo slideshow (one photo — a static frame, several — looping through); Fill/Fit framing; “keep video sound”. Intro and outro — bumpers from the gallery, glued as is (a 2–10s logo intro, a “subscribe” outro).

Subtitles: Word by word / Karaoke / Plain text / Off; position bottom/centre/top; the “style preferences” field (colour, font, outline) — with a live preview on the frame. Music plays softly under the voice (volume %, optionally only the first N seconds). Overlay — a transparent PNG per format (logo, frame, caption); subtitles are drawn above the overlay. Progress bar — a thin timer at the top of the frame: shows the video is short and keeps viewers to the end.
examples: Several product photos → “Photo slideshow” — footage without any filming.
“Word by word” subtitles + the wish “yellow, bold, with outline” — the style shows up right on the preview.
Add a 2–3s logo intro bumper and a “subscribe” outro.
A PNG frame with your logo for 9:16 + the progress bar — a branded look for every clip.

publisher.title: Publisher — auto-posting
publisher.excerpt: Posts and chains to 9 social networks via Blotato: schedule, auto-series, AI captions.
publisher.lead: The Publisher sends clips to 9 networks: TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X (Twitter), Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky, Pinterest. The provider is Blotato on the bring-your-own-key model: posts go through your own Blotato account. Inside the tab: Feed · Calendar · My schedule · Analytics plus the “New post” studio.

setup.title: Connecting (one time)
setup.body: 1) Paste your Blotato key in Settings → the Generation tab (the Blotato card; “Check” calls the API live). 2) Connect your social accounts in the Blotato dashboard (my.blotato.com/settings) — the network tiles in the Publisher open exactly the right dashboard page. 3) Connected accounts appear in the Publisher as toggles — choose where each post or chain goes.
examples: Settings → Generation → Blotato: paste the key and press “Check”.
Click the TikTok tile in the Publisher — the TikTok connection page of the Blotato dashboard opens.
Connect several accounts of one network — each appears as its own toggle.

post.title: “New post” — a one-off publication
post.body:
The post studio: media from the Gallery, text with per-network limit counters (X 280, Bluesky 300, TikTok/Instagram 2200, YouTube/Facebook 5000…), text tabs “All” + a per-platform version ✎, a thread for X/Threads/Bluesky (an empty line = the next thread post).

✦ AI caption (Claude): pick a tone — you get A/B variants, per-network versions, hashtags and a YouTube title; if the clip has a breakdown, the AI uses its DNA. There are text templates. Platform options: TikTok privacy + the “AI-generated” flag, YouTube privacy + “notify subscribers”, Instagram type (Reel), Pinterest boards. “When”: Now / Date-time / Next slot (the nearest window of “My schedule”).
examples: Pick a clip → “✦ AI caption” with the “engaging” tone → A/B variants with hashtags.
Open the ✎ tab for X — shorten the text to the 280 limit; other networks keep the full version.
An empty line in the thread field — that’s how a post thread is built for X/Threads/Bluesky.
The “Next slot” mode — the post takes the nearest window of your schedule by itself.

slots.title: “My schedule” — slots
slots.body: Slots are your weekly posting grid: day of week + time (entered and shown in local time, stored in UTC). Slots are the backbone of auto-posting: chains and the “Next slot” mode fill them. Series are laid out up to 35 days ahead — enough for a month-long series.
examples: Set Mon/Wed/Fri 19:00 — a standard 3-posts-a-week grid.
Add several slots per day (9:00 and 19:00) — chains fill both windows.
A series of 12 clips with 3 slots a week stretches a month ahead (35-day horizon).

chains.title: Chains: manual series and the autopilot
chains.body:
Manual series: tick several finished clips in the Gallery → “Publish N” → the series is laid out over the free slots of your schedule right away. Caption per clip: AI (tone and language), a fixed text or the file name.

Auto chain: once a minute the scheduler takes a fresh unpublished autopilot clip (the “Auto” sub-filter of the UGC tab) → generates a caption with the Post engine (without a Claude key a fallback kicks in — the chain never stalls) → puts it into the nearest free slot. Settings: a daily cap (default 3), a format filter (a 9:16 chain posts only vertical clips — to TikTok/Reels; a 16:9 chain only horizontal — to YouTube: they never compete for files), auto-pause after 3 fails in a row, per-chain status counters.

The full conveyor: Trends (scheduled auto-analysis) → a UGC template → “Auto” clips → an auto chain → social networks. Set it up once — content ships itself.
examples: Multi-select 10 clips in the Gallery → “Publish 10” — a month-long series over your slots.
Create 2 auto chains: 9:16 → TikTok+Reels and 16:9 → YouTube — the files never overlap.
Daily cap = 2 — the chain won’t flood the feed even if the autopilot produced more.
3 fails in a row — the chain pauses itself and shows the last error.
Enable auto-analysis in Trends + attach a UGC template + enable the chain — the conveyor is ready.

feed.title: Feed, calendar, retries, analytics
feed.body: Feed — all posts with statuses and links to what got published. Failed submissions go to auto-retries (backoff 2 → 4 → 8 minutes, up to 3 attempts); in-flight statuses refresh in the background even when the tab is closed. Calendar — the whole week: move or cancel scheduled posts. Analytics — X/Instagram/Facebook/Threads/Bluesky metrics from Blotato; for TikTok and YouTube use the “Channels” tab of Trends.
examples: A post failed on a network hiccup — leave it: the retry re-sends in 2–8 minutes.
In the calendar, drag a post to another day or cancel it before it goes out.
Watch X/IG/FB reach right in the Publisher; TikTok/YouTube — in “Channels”.

storyboard.title: Storyboard
storyboard.excerpt: Auto-edit a Reel from a talking video: transcription → storyboard → generation → assembly.
storyboard.lead: Storyboard re-edits a finished “talking” video into a dynamic Reel using a professional editing-conveyor mechanic: transcription → chunks of ≤8 s → a storyboard of up to 6 panels per chunk → generation → assembly. Open it from the Gallery: the Storyboard tab → the “New storyboard” tile (a video from the Gallery or an upload from your device) or an existing project card. The studio is a 5-station stepper; the pipeline is frugal: transcription — 1 Gemini request, the AI panel plan — 1 Claude request, and the software render engine is free.

overview.title: What it is and how to open it
overview.body:
The idea: you already have a video of a person talking (your take, a trend, a UGC clip) — Storyboard turns it into an edited Reel with shot changes, titles and cutaways. A project lives as a card on the Gallery’s Storyboard tab (the cover is the first panel’s frame, plus status and chunk count); clicking opens the studio with 5 stations: Source → Transcription → Storyboard → Generation → Assembly.

Pipeline discipline: only chunk 1 is generated and reviewed first — the rest unlock after it. That protects your keys and time: a mistake is cheaper to catch on the first chunk.
examples: Gallery → Storyboard → “New storyboard” → pick a video from the Gallery or upload a file.
Take your own footage from Media files or a downloaded trend from Trends.
The project card shows the status (“Storyboard ready · N chunks”) — click to continue.

transcribe.title: Source and Transcription
transcribe.body: At the Transcription station Gemini watches the whole video: verbatim speech with timecodes plus real scene changes. The clip is then cut into chunks of up to 8 seconds at phrase ends — chunks never tear words apart, and 8 seconds is the Google Flow generation limit. There is a mini-player of the source and a fallback path — “No AI (even chunks)” — equal slices without transcription.
examples: Press “Transcribe and storyboard” — one Gemini request for the whole clip.
Check the line texts against the timecodes — titles and subtitles follow them.
No Gemini key? “No AI (even chunks)” still slices the clip without a transcription.

board.title: Storyboard — panels and frames
board.body:
Each chunk holds up to 6 panels; the types: Close-up speaker · Full-screen title · Cutaway · Split screen · Mockup · Final + CTA. The plan is built by the Claude director (the “Replan AI” button; without a key a template fallback kicks in). Every panel has a timing, a caption and a live preview: titles render exactly as in the clip (wysiwyg, in the style preset’s colour).

The chunk’s filmstrip — a strip of frames (~every 0.7 s) with a coloured bar of panel boundaries: select a panel and click a frame on the strip — it becomes that panel’s frame. The “Assemble PNG storyboard” button builds a grid of all panels as one image — checking the storyboard with your eyes is cheaper before generation than after.
examples: “Replan AI” — Claude re-lays the chunk into panels to match your speech.
Change a panel’s type in the dropdown — e.g. “Cutaway” instead of “Close-up speaker”.
Click a frame on the filmstrip — assign the panel an exact frame (say, the movement peak).
“Assemble PNG storyboard” — the whole storyboard as one image for review.

engines.title: Generation — three engines
engines.body: Software (ffmpeg) — free, no external keys: camera push-ins on the speaker, titles, split screens — everything is built programmatically from your source. Omni Flash API (≈$1 per chunk, a Gemini key): the chunk’s starting frame “comes alive” following a per-second prompt built from the panels; the output is fitted to 1080×1920 with the chunk’s original voice on top. Flow extension (a Google Flow subscription, no API keys): semi-auto — the studio prepares the chunk + a PNG storyboard + a prompt, you generate in Google Flow and press “Attach result”; automatic — the “Send all chunks to Flow” button: the queue goes to the extension, it uploads the references and starts the generations itself, and a watcher attaches the finished clips (with the original voice) and shows queue badges.
examples: Start with the software engine — fast, free and keyless.
Omni Flash API — a living shot instead of a static cut (≈$1 per chunk).
Flow automatic: keep the labs.google/flow tab open — the chunks generate themselves in turn.
Chunk 1 first: review the result, then the remaining chunks unlock.

assemble.title: Assembly — badge, CTA, subtitles
assemble.body: The Assembly station glues the enabled chunks into one Reel. Options: a corner badge (e.g. @mychannel), a CTA code word (use the same word in the post caption — viewers type it in the comments), and subtitles from the transcription (a checkbox). Auto-assembly: once every enabled chunk is ready, the clip assembles itself (on by default). The result goes to the Gallery — from there send it to the Publisher.
